findings.title: Preserve the light-theme color of embedded-post author links
findings.body: The light-theme branch changes the embedded-post author link from 30% to 70% lightness instead of preserving the existing value. This makes the author substantially paler on the light background and reduces readability (with a #222 primary and white background, the new color has roughly 1.9:1 contrast). Keep the light branch at 30% and use the complementary 70% secondary value for the dark branch.

findings.title: Retain the distinct color for group-member names
findings.body: The group-member name previously used 30% primary lightness, but now uses 50%, exactly like the adjacent title. This unintentionally fades names in light themes and removes the existing visual distinction between the member's name and title. The same regression appears in mobile/user.scss at line 497. Preserve 30% for the light branch and use 70% secondary lightness for the dark branch in both files.

findings.title: Preserve the stronger light-theme color for topic-map headings
findings.body: The mobile topic-map h3 changes from 20% primary lightness to 50% in the light-theme branch. It now has the same faded color as h4, weakening the heading hierarchy and reducing text contrast even when no dark theme is enabled. The desktop equivalent correctly retains 20%/80%; use that pair here as well so this dark-theme fix does not regress light-theme headings.
